purpose: test whether the state-conditioned interaction mechanism inferred from the original 14M instance repeats across fresh tokenizer-safe synthetic instances and stage lengths

codebook_seed_derivation.method: first four big-endian uint32 words of SHA256(label)
codebook_seed_derivation.label: chronotrace-t2-independent-codebooks-v1

stage_randomness.rule: stage-specific seed is reset on every stage-map invocation so stochasticity cannot encode macro position

pre_registered_checks.check_1: for each seed, if a first full-order failure occurs within the sampled lengths, at least one shared-prefix tail robustness value is <= 0 at that first failure
pre_registered_checks.check_2: across all errors in the map, at least 75 percent preserve the first stage and differ from truth only by swapping positions 2 and 3
pre_registered_checks.check_3: after full-order failures begin, first-stage recovery remains higher than full-order recovery in at least three of four independent codebooks
pre_registered_checks.check_4: report, without selection, whether increasing stage length tends to reduce base/conditioned commutator alignment and increase relative commutator drift

selection_rule: none; all four codebooks and all six stage lengths must be reported regardless of outcome
scale_decision: 31M remains blocked until T2 is interpreted and the theory is revised or retained
